<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

<!-- Summarize the change in 1-2 lines. Link relevant issues and PRs. -->

Reject sweep figure groups that would write to the same PNG after filename sanitization, before starting plotting jobs.

Related to #60794 and #60795, but scoped to figure outputs: #60795 protects benchmark result/cache directories and does not validate the paths produced by `--fig-by`.

## Claims

<!-- State the accomplishments in a few concrete bullets: speedups, feature support, bug fixes, etc. -->

- Reject conflicting figure paths in both normal plotting and `--dry-run`.
- Preserve existing non-conflicting filenames and allow collisions removed by per-figure filters.
- Cover the real plotting CLI, including valid PNG output, without starting a model or server.

## Validation

<!-- Show evidence that the claims are met by this change, and steps to reproduce validations. -->

Validated on Windows x86_64 with Python 3.12.15, CPU-only Torch 2.14.0, NumPy 2.2.6, pandas 2.2.3, and the repository-pinned Ruff 0.14.0 / mypy 1.20.2.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| New CLI tests with original production code at `e9acf48614` | 2 failed, 2 passed; both failures show duplicate paths accepted |
| Patched CLI tests plus existing plot-filter tests | 38 passed |
| Python 3.11 type-check target | Passed, 2 source files |
| Repository hooks | Python, docs, typos, oldest-Python mypy, SPDX, import checks, and Buildkite test tethering passed |
| Full hook invocation | Exit 1 only because the unrelated Docker graph hook requires absolute `/bin/bash` on Windows |
| Same Docker graph script invoked with Git Bash | Passed with the actual staged filenames; Dockerfile is unchanged |
| Commit-time hooks | All other checks passed; only the unsupported Docker launcher was skipped after its script passed directly |
| October 30 import-hoisting follow-up | 38 focused tests passed again; scoped Ruff and Python 3.11 mypy passed |
| Optional-dependency smoke check | Real CLI dry-run with filters passed with pandas, matplotlib, and seaborn imports unavailable |

Run from this branch with the isolated uv environment active:

```powershell
# Original production code plus the new regression file: 2 failed, 2 passed.
uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests\benchmarks tests\benchmarks\sweep\test_plot.py -q

# Patched production code: 38 passed.
uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests\benchmarks tests\benchmarks\sweep\test_plot.py tests\benchmarks\test_plot_filters.py -q

# Passed.
uv run --active --no-project mypy --python-version 3.11 --follow-imports silent vllm\benchmarks\sweep\plot.py tests\benchmarks\sweep\test_plot.py

# Relevant checks passed; the full invocation has the Windows launcher limitation above.
$env:PYTHONUTF8 = "1"
uv run --active --no-project pre-commit run

# Passed using the installed Git Bash.
& 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe' (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath '.\tools\pre_commit\update-dockerfile-graph.sh').Path @(git --no-pager diff --cached --name-only)
```

Git Bash's `bin` and `usr\bin` directories were on `PATH` for repository hooks. Source-only imports emit the expected warning about missing generated version metadata. No model, serving, GPU, or performance evaluation was run; those execution paths are unchanged.

## Details

<!-- Explain motivation, design decisions, root cause, tradeoffs, and limitations concisely. Link or collapse lengthy supporting material. -->

Distinct labels such as `case/a` and `case_a` produce the same figure filename. Previously, separate plotting workers could write to that shared destination.

The preflight groups figure jobs by their existing generated paths. For potentially conflicting paths, it respects the existing per-group filters so an empty group does not reserve a destination. An error is raised if multiple nonempty groups still share a path. Valid filenames are not renamed, and no dependencies are added.

The [review follow-up](https://github.com/singh4jitendra/vllm/commit/bffe08fe82aae50a0575d8689aa84d7790d1c091) moves optional pandas setup above the per-path loop, as [requested by dilberx](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63468#discussion_r4424252115). Setup runs once, and only when filters and colliding paths require it; ordinary dry-runs retain their optional-dependency behavior.

Duplicate checks on October 24 inspected the current issue discussion, matching open PRs, and the changed-file scope of #60795. Its result-directory guard does not cover PNG figure destinations; this change leaves benchmark planning and cached results untouched.

Before the original submission, the human submitter confirmed reviewing the original patch and running its documented tests, and explicitly authorized the personal GitHub noreply DCO sign-off and required assistance attribution. The author subsequently requested the review follow-up; its validation is recorded above.

files.patch:
@@ -243,6 +243,11 @@ vllm bench sweep plot $EXPERIMENT_DIR \
 !!! tip
     You can use `--dry-run` to preview the figures to be plotted.
 
+!!! important
+    Figure groups must produce distinct filenames after sanitization. For example, labels `case/a` and `case_a` map to the same filename.
+    Plotting rejects such collisions before creating figures, including with `--dry-run`, rather than overwriting one group's output.
+    Groups with no matching rows after `--filter-by` do not cause a collision.
+
 ### Pareto chart
 
 `vllm bench sweep plot_pareto` helps pick configurations that balance per-user and per-GPU throughput.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import argparse
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.benchmarks.sweep.plot import SweepPlotArgs, main
+from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
+
+
+def _plot_args(
+    experiment_dir: Path, names: tuple[str, str], *extra_args: str
+) -> argparse.Namespace:
+    records = [
+        {
+            "_benchmark_name": name,
+            "total_token_throughput": 100 + index,
+            "median_ttft_ms": 10 + index,
+        }
+        for index, name in enumerate(names)
+    ]
+    (experiment_dir / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(records), encoding="utf-8")
+    parser = SweepPlotArgs.add_cli_args(FlexibleArgumentParser())
+    return parser.parse_args(
+        [
+            str(experiment_dir),
+            "--fig-by",
+            "_benchmark_name",
+            "--fig-dir",
+            "figures",
+            "--no-error-bars",
+            *extra_args,
+        ]
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("names", [("case/a", "case_a"), ("case..a", "case__a")])
+def test_cli_rejects_colliding_figure_paths(
+    tmp_path: Path, names: tuple[str, str]
+) -> None:
+    args = _plot_args(tmp_path, names, "--dry-run")
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="same figure output path"):
+        main(args)
+
+    assert not (tmp_path / "figures").exists()
+
+
+def test_cli_preserves_distinct_figure_paths(
+    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setenv("MPLBACKEND", "Agg")
+
+    main(_plot_args(tmp_path, ("case_a", "case_b")))
+
+    figures = sorted((tmp_path / "figures").glob("*.png"))
+    assert [figure.name for figure in figures] == [
+        "FIGURE-_benchmark_name=case_a.png",
+        "FIGURE-_benchmark_name=case_b.png",
+    ]
+    assert all(
+        figure.read_bytes().startswith(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n") for figure in figures
+    )
+
+
+def test_cli_allows_collisions_removed_by_filter(
+    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setenv("MPLBACKEND", "Agg")
+    args = _plot_args(
+        tmp_path,
+        ("case/a", "case_a"),
+        "--filter-by",
+        "_benchmark_name==case_a",
+    )
+
+    main(args)
+
+    figures = list((tmp_path / "figures").glob("*.png"))
+    assert [figure.name for figure in figures] == ["FIGURE-_benchmark_name=case_a.png"]
+    assert figures[0].read_bytes().startswith(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
